hits.title: Gunnebo Entrance Control acquires Shuretech Ltd | Security Matters
hits.snippet: **Brian Sims** Editor GUNNEBO ENTRANCE Control has acquired Shuretech Ltd in order to combine established field engineering expertise and a proven service-led operating model within its UK business. Founded back in 2011, Shuretech Ltd has built its reputation on the installation, maintenance and lifecycle support of gates, barriers, turnstiles, doors and shutters across the South East of England. The company is recognised for its technically skilled engineers, structured preventative maintenance programmes and responsive fault resolution. Carl Graham and Lewis Hakesley, the joint owners of Shuretech Ltd, said: “Service quality and technical competence have always been central to our business. Our engineers work closely with customers to ensure systems operate safely and effectively throughout their lifecycle. hits.snippet: Assa Abloy has agreed to acquire Gunnebo Entrance Control to add a portfolio of speed gates, automated fare gates, full-height turnstiles, and retail entrance controls that can connect biometric identity checks with the physical movement of people. Assa Abloy has agreed to acquire Gunnebo Entrance Control to add a portfolio of speed gates, automated fare gates, full-height turnstiles, and retail entrance controls that can connect biometric identity checks with the physical movement of people. Gunnebo Entrance Control will become part of the Pedestrian segment within Assa Abloy’s Entrance Systems division. The company says the acquisition will complement its existing pedestrian access portfolio and expand its ability to provide efficient entrance systems. Headquartered in Maresfield, UK, the acquired business has roughly 670 people employed. Gunnebo Entrance Control generated about US$172 million in sales in 2025. Assa Abloy says the company has a good EBIT margin, but the acquisition will initially have a small dilutive effect on earnings per share.
